definitions.explanation: The individual elements that together make up a whole. Used across fields — grammar, chemistry, software, systems engineering, social theory — to refer to the parts of which something is composed.

examples.japanese: {重要|じゅうよう}な{構成要素|こうせいようそ}。
{家族|かぞく}は{社会|しゃかい}の{基本的|きほんてき}な{構成要素|こうせいようそ}だ。
examples.english: The family is a fundamental component of society.

examples.japanese: タンパク{質|しつ}は{生命|せいめい}の{最|もっと}も{重要|じゅうよう}な{構成要素|こうせいようそ}の{一|ひと}つである。
examples.english: Proteins are one of the most important constituent elements of life.

examples.japanese: このシステムは{複数|ふくすう}の{構成要素|こうせいようそ}から{成|な}り{立|た}っており、それぞれが{特定|とくてい}の{役割|やくわり}を{担|にな}っている。
examples.english: This system consists of multiple components, each of which plays a specific role.

notes:
Compound of {構成|こうせい} ('composition; structure') and {要素|ようそ} ('element; factor'). A set expression meaning 'the elements that make up the composition' — i.e., the parts of a whole.

USAGE:
Standard technical and academic vocabulary. Common across natural sciences, social sciences, engineering, and grammar. Often used with から{成|な}り{立|た}つ ('to be composed of') or から{構成|こうせい}される ('to be constituted by').

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {重要|じゅうよう}な{構成要素|こうせいようそ}: an important component
- {基本的|きほんてき}な{構成要素|こうせいようそ}: a fundamental component
- {主|おも}な{構成要素|こうせいようそ}: the main components
- {構成要素|こうせいようそ}を{分析|ぶんせき}する: to analyze the components
- {構成要素|こうせいようそ}に{分解|ぶんかい}する: to break down into components
- {構成要素|こうせいようそ}の{一|ひと}つ: one of the components
- 〜の{構成要素|こうせいようそ}となる: to constitute a component of ~

SIMILAR WORDS:
- {要素|ようそ}: element; factor — broader; can include abstract factors
- {成分|せいぶん}: ingredient; chemical component — specifically for substances, food, medicine
- {部品|ぶひん}: part; component part — physical parts of machines or products
- コンポーネント: component — English loanword; used in IT and engineering
- {構成|こうせい}: composition; structure — the act or result of composing
- {因子|いんし}: factor — used in mathematics, statistics, genetics
